findings.rationale: HI's local AUC is far below the federation (about 0.61 vs pooled 0.79; z about -6.1), with ECE z about +9.9 and CITL z about -8.3. Its observed prevalence (0.27) is about twice what its features imply (mean predicted 0.13), and its O/E ratio is about 2.0-2.5 in both sex subgroups. The pattern is a degraded, over-positive label set rather than a clean prevalence shift, since AUC is also collapsed. Its updates are anomalous as well: mean cosine to the median update is -0.71 (z about -8.2), and the median norm ratio is 4.76 (z about +8.2). Prevalence is already elevated in round 1, so I date the onset to round 1.

NE has the lowest local AUC in the federation (about 0.58; z about -6.9), with ECE z about +10.5 and CITL z about -8.6. Its observed prevalence is about 0.30 against a mean prediction of 0.155, and its positive rate in AgeGroup 2.0 (0.47) is far above the federation median (0.02). Its updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.71 (z about -8.2) and median norm ratio 5.69 (z about +7.5). The elevated prevalence is present in round 1, so onset is round 1.

UT's local AUC is about 0.58 (z about -7.0), with ECE z about +10.7 and CITL z about -8.3. Its observed prevalence is about 0.26 against a mean prediction of 0.12, and its O/E ratio is about 2.5 in the male and female subgroups. Its updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.71 (z about -8.3) and median norm ratio 5.33 (z about +8.2). The pattern matches HI and NE and is present from round 1, so onset is round 1.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed with narrower queries. Three clients (HI, NE, UT) stand apart on every relevant screen. Their local AUC is about 0.58–0.61 against about 0.79 pooled, their CITL is about -0.14, and their observed prevalence is roughly double what their predictions imply. Their updates point against the median with 5x norm inflation. Because local performance is degraded, not normal, I classed these as label_noise rather than poisoning. Their elevated prevalence is present from round 1. Not reported: CT's GenHlth tail anomaly, which did not reproduce on re-query (p99 4.995, normal). DC (DiffWalk drift, z about 3.9), GU (small-client norm ratio, z about 3.8) and scattered AgeGroup subgroup outliers in small cells are below the reporting threshold and look like noise from small sites. Budget is fully spent (0.0 left). Attribution churn and global performance were not queried, so explanation_instability and global-level trends were not checked.
